blocks.text: 1. IVF-PQ
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447303200-547871145.png
IVF-PQ covers how IVF combines with compression for even greater efficiency, layering a second technique on top of clustering.
It layers compressed vector representations on top of IVF's clustering, combining both techniques into a single efficiency strategy.
2. Two Techniques Combined
IVF narrows which vectors get compared; product quantization shrinks how much each comparison costs.
Combining both techniques attacks the search problem from two different angles at once.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Technique","What it optimizes"],"rows":[["IVF","Which vectors get compared at all"],["Product quantization","How cheap each individual comparison is"]]}

blocks.text: 3. Why IVF Alone Still Has Cost

blocks.alt: Why IVF Alone Still Has Cost
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447303201-646697219.png
Even after narrowing to a few clusters, each remaining comparison still uses full precision vectors.
Those remaining comparisons still cost real memory and compute.
4. Product Quantization In Brief
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447303201-990529159.png
Product quantization gets its own full dedicated topic immediately after this one.
This section previews just enough of it to explain how it combines with IVF specifically.
5. Compressing Vectors Within Clusters
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447303201-674884672.png
Vectors inside each IVF cluster get stored in a compressed, quantized form instead of full precision.
This dramatically reduces how much memory the entire index actually requires.
6. Fast Approximate Distances Within Clusters
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447303202-10389248.png
Comparing compressed vectors uses precomputed lookup tables instead of full distance formulas.
This makes each individual comparison inside a cluster faster too, not just smaller.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: Precomputed lookup tables let IVF-PQ estimate a distance with a handful of table lookups and additions, far cheaper than computing a full precision distance formula for every candidate.

blocks.text: 7. The Accuracy Cost Of Compounding Approximation
IVF-PQ stacks two separate sources of approximation together.
Clustering can miss boundary neighbors, and compression adds further imprecision on top.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: IVF-PQ combines the edge boundary problem from IVF with the accuracy loss from compression, meaning its overall recall tends to be somewhat lower than either technique used alone.

blocks.text: 8. Memory Savings At Scale
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447303202-9351334.png
Much like the storage efficiency gained from sparsity in Sparse Embeddings, IVF-PQ can shrink an index's memory footprint by an order of magnitude.
This makes collections that would not fit in memory otherwise become practical.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Index type","Relative memory footprint"],"rows":[["Full precision IVF","Baseline, full size"],["IVF-PQ","Often an order of magnitude smaller"]]}

blocks.text: 9. Recognizing When IVF-PQ Is Worth Its Added Complexity

blocks.alt: Recognizing When IVF-PQ Is Worth Its Added Complexity
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447303203-828888754.png
Extremely large collections with tight memory budgets benefit most from IVF-PQ.
Smaller collections where accuracy matters most may prefer plain IVF or HNSW instead.
10. Worked Example
The example below demonstrates the memory savings from compressing vectors within IVF clusters.

code.content:
num_vectors = 1_000_000
dimensions = 128
bytes_per_float = 4  # full precision 32 bit float
bytes_per_pq_code = 8  # a compact quantized code per vector

full_precision_bytes = num_vectors * dimensions * bytes_per_float
pq_compressed_bytes = num_vectors * bytes_per_pq_code

full_precision_mb = full_precision_bytes / (1024 * 1024)
pq_compressed_mb = pq_compressed_bytes / (1024 * 1024)

print(f"Full precision IVF storage: {full_precision_mb:,.1f} MB")
print(f"IVF-PQ compressed storage: {pq_compressed_mb:,.1f} MB")
print(f"Memory reduction: {(1 - pq_compressed_mb / full_precision_mb) * 100:.1f}%")

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: Running this example shows the compressed IVF-PQ storage requiring only a small fraction of the full precision baseline, at the cost of the compounded approximation discussed above.

blocks.text: 11. Common Mistakes

items: Choosing IVF-PQ for a small collection where the accuracy tradeoff outweighs its memory benefits.
Forgetting that IVF-PQ compounds two separate sources of approximation error, not just one.
Assuming IVF-PQ recall matches plain IVF or HNSW without measuring the actual difference.
Skipping product quantization's own dedicated topic before assuming full understanding of IVF-PQ.

blocks.text: 12. Key Takeaways

items: IVF-PQ layers compressed vector representations on top of IVF's clustering.
IVF narrows which vectors get compared; product quantization shrinks how much each comparison costs.
Even after narrowing to a few clusters, full precision comparisons still cost real memory and compute.
Vectors inside each cluster get stored in a compressed, quantized form to reduce memory.
Comparing compressed vectors uses precomputed lookup tables instead of full distance formulas.
IVF-PQ stacks clustering approximation and compression approximation, compounding accuracy loss.
IVF-PQ can shrink an index's memory footprint by an order of magnitude at large scale.
Extremely large collections with tight memory budgets benefit most from this combined approach.
